question.problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=4,$ $y=0,$ $y=1,$ $z=1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=y\sqrt{x}\,i+(z-x)\,j+{y}^{3}\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\sqrt{x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z-x)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}}+0+0 \\  & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}z \\  & =[\sqrt{x}]_{x=1}^{x=4}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\cdot (2-1) \\  & =(2-1)\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
